record.paper_title: Open Questions in CMR Manganites, Relevance of Clustered States, and Analogies with other Compounds
record.original_question: How can the theory of phase separation in manganites be made quantitative enough to compute the temperature dependence of d.c. resistivity in a percolative scenario and yield a simple predictive formula rather than only qualitative or network-based agreement with experiments?

evidence.quote: The theory of phase separation should be made more quantitative. Can a rough temperature dependence of the d.c. resistivity be calculated within the percolative scenario? Certainly we already have resistor-network calculations that match the experiments, but not a simple anybody-can-use formula.

artifact.status_search_result: The problem of deriving a simple closed-form predictive formula for the d.c. resistivity ρ(T) of phase-separated manganites in a percolative scenario remains an open research direction. Subsequent works (effective-medium approximations, two-fluid models, random resistor networks by Mayr, Moreo, Dagotto and others) provide approximate or numerical descriptions, but no universally accepted simple analytic formula derived from a fully quantitative phase-separation theory has been established.

status_evidence.title: Phase Separation Scenario for Manganese Oxides and Related Materials
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews phase-separation and percolative transport in manganites with resistor-network style modeling.
status_evidence.claim: Percolative transport in manganites is typically treated via resistor-network simulations rather than a simple closed-form ρ(T).

status_evidence.title: Resistor network models of CMR manganites (Mayr et al.)
status_evidence.snippet: Numerical resistor-network calculations reproduce CMR features from phase-separated clusters.
status_evidence.claim: Existing quantitative agreement comes from network simulations, not analytic formulas.
